title: Justifying faith believes in God: trust, hope of pardon, and love (Trent sess. 6)
source_text: XLIII. Itaque non aliam fidem justificare docent, quam illam qua, non tantum Deo, sed etiam in Deum credimus, id est, quae junctam habet fiduciam in Deum, & spem veniae ab eo obtinendae. Unde nascitur Dei amor & dilectio, ut colligere est ex ipso Concilio Tridentino, sess. 6. cap. 6. Disponuntur autem, inquit, ad ipsam justitiam, dum excitati divina gratia, & adjuti, fidem ex auditu concipientes, libere moventur in Deum, credentes vera esse quae divinitus revelata & promissa sunt, atque illud in primis, a Deo justificari impium per gratiam ejus, per redemptionem, quae est in Christo Jesu; & dum peccatores se esse intelligentes, a divinae justitiae timore, quo utiliter concutiuntur, ad considerandam Dei misericordiam se convertendo, in spem eriguntur, fidentes Deum sibi propter Christum propitium fore, illumque tanquam omnis justitiae fontem, diligere incipiunt, &c.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore they teach that no other faith justifies than that by which we believe not only God, but also in God—that is, which has joined to it trust in God and hope of pardon to be obtained from him. From which arises love and delight in God, as may be gathered from the Council of Trent itself, session 6, chapter 6. But they are disposed, it says, toward that very righteousness, while stirred by divine grace and helped, conceiving faith from hearing, they are freely moved toward God, believing those things to be true which have been divinely revealed and promised, and that especially, that the ungodly is justified by God through his grace, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus; and while understanding themselves to be sinners, from fear of divine justice by which they are usefully shaken, turning themselves to consider God's mercy, they are raised into hope, trusting that God will be propitious to them for Christ's sake, and begin to love him as the fountain of all righteousness, etc.
pass_b_english: Justifying faith is believing in God: trust and hope of pardon, from which love arises.
Trent sess. 6 ch. 6: grace-stirred disposition toward righteousness through faith, fear, hope, love.
